findings.evidence: With an injected SafeFetcher (resolver -> 93.184.216.34, MockTransport, fetch_url extra_types), FetchUrlTool().execute(request_text='http://bücher.de/') and 'http://xn--bcher-kva.de/' both return {'status':'unavailable','message':'URI could not reach that URL.','error':'UNREACHABLE'} and nothing reaches the transport. httpx.URL('http://xn--bcher-kva.de/').host == 'bücher.de' while NP.check_url(...).host == 'xn--bcher-kva.de', so _Pinned.handle_request raises ConnectError('PIN_HOST_MISMATCH') (reproduced directly with httpx 0.28.1). The baseline fetched these hosts with requests.get. The failure is closed and honest, and IDN hosts are rare, so LOW.
findings.suggested_fix: In _Pinned.handle_request compare the ASCII host, e.g. request.url.raw_host.decode('ascii').lower() != self.host, and add an IDN test in tests/ssrf and tests/web.
findings.title: fetch_url can no longer fetch internationalised (IDN) host names: SafeFetcher's pin check compares httpx's Unicode host with netpolicy's punycode host

findings.evidence: A public response with content-type text/html and content-encoding: gzip returns {'status':'unsupported','message':"URI has no reader for content type 'unknown'.",'content_type':''}. The baseline (requests: Accept */*, gzip decoded) returned the page text. The new Accept header also lists no document types (application/pdf, docx, xlsx, csv) and no */*, so servers that strictly negotiate on Accept could answer 406 for documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Let SafeFetcher callers pass an Accept value (fetch_url adds its document types or */*), and map a CONTENT_ENCODING_* refusal_code in fetch_url to a clear message instead of 'unknown' content type; or document both as accepted behaviour changes.
findings.title: fetch_url now sends W1's Accept / Accept-Encoding: identity; a server that gzips anyway gets a misleading 'unsupported, unknown content type'
